## Defensible v1 for a 12‑Hospital Sepsis‑Risk CDSS Rollout *(per‑seat annual subscription)* Below is a step‑by‑step blueprint that balances **clinical safety**, **legal & regulatory exposure**, and **financial structure** while keeping the rollout realistic for a mid‑sized health system. The goal is to launch a production‑ready product that can be audited, updated, and scaled without exposing the organization to undue risk. --- ### 1. Clinical Safety – “What must work before we go live?” | Phase | Key Activities | Deliverables / Metrics | |-------|----------------|------------------------| | **A. Baseline & Retrospective Validation** | • Pull historic EHR data (≥ 2 yrs) for all 12 sites.
• Run the model on this cohort to compute sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV at several thresholds.
• Compare against gold‑standard sepsis adjudication (chart review or ICD‑10 codes). | • Validation report with performance curves.
• Threshold recommendation that balances early detection vs alert fatigue. | | **B. Prospective Pilot** | • Deploy in 2–3 pilot sites (mixed acuity, geography).
• Run “shadow mode” – generate scores but do not act on them.
• Collect provider feedback via surveys & focus groups.
• Monitor real‑time metrics: alert volume, override rate, time to intervention. | • Pilot performance dashboard.
• Qualitative report of workflow fit and usability. | | **C. Integration & Workflow Design** | • Embed score in the EHR (e.g., as a “Sepsis Risk” panel).
• Define default alert triggers (e.g., ≥ 70 % risk → pop‑up + order set).
• Build “override” and “dismiss” logging. | • UI mock‑ups.
• EHR integration test scripts. | | **D. Training & Change Management** | • Create concise training videos, cheat sheets, and FAQ for each provider role.
• Conduct live Q&A sessions (virtual or in‑person).
• Deploy a “champion” program at each site. | • Attendance logs.
• Post‑training competency quiz scores. | | **E. Continuous Monitoring & Drift Management** | • Set up automated dashboards that flag:
 - Sudden drops in sensitivity/specificity.
 - Shifts in patient demographics or vital sign distributions.
 - Alert fatigue (e.g., > 30% dismiss rate).
• Define a “Model Review Board” to approve updates. | • Monthly monitoring report.
• Change‑control log. | | **F. Incident Response** | • Create SOP for false positives/negatives that lead to adverse events.
• Include escalation path: Clinical Lead → Risk Management → Legal. | • Incident response playbook. | --- ### 2. Legal & Regulatory Exposure – “What must we satisfy?” | Domain | Key Requirements | Practical Steps | |--------|------------------|-----------------| | **FDA / SaMD** | • The tool is a *Software as a Medical Device* (SaMD) that influences clinical decisions.
• Likely Class II (moderate risk).
• Must meet FDA guidance on AI/ML medical devices (e.g., “Proposed Regulatory Framework for Modifying Software in SaMD”). | • Prepare a **510(k)** submission or seek *de‑novo* clearance.
• Include: intended use, performance data, risk analysis, post‑market surveillance plan.
• If the vendor already holds FDA clearance, obtain a **“Use Agreement”** that transfers liability to the vendor for the specific implementation. | | **HIPAA / Privacy** | • All patient data used for model training and inference must be protected.
• Must have Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with any third‑party cloud or analytics provider. | • Conduct a HIPAA risk assessment.
• Ensure all data is de‑identified when possible; otherwise, use secure encrypted storage and access controls. | | **Data Governance** | • Consent: If the model uses patient data beyond what is normally used for care (e.g., research), obtain IRB approval or opt‑in consent. | • Add a “Use of Data” clause in the EHR terms of service.
• Document all data lineage and audit trails. | | **Malpractice & Liability** | • Providers may be sued if the tool misleads them.
• The health system must protect itself via indemnification clauses in vendor contracts. | • Include a *“No‑Fault”* clause that limits liability to the subscription fee, unless gross negligence is proven.
• Require the vendor to carry professional liability insurance covering AI errors. | | **Cybersecurity** | • Must comply with NIST SP 800‑53 and ISO 27001 for medical software. | • Conduct a penetration test before go‑live.
• Implement role‑based access, MFA, audit logs, and incident response. | | **Reimbursement & Billing** | • Currently no CPT code for AI CDSS; however, the tool may be bundled into existing sepsis bundle codes (e.g., 99495). | • Track usage metrics to support future reimbursement claims.
• Maintain documentation of clinical benefit for payer negotiations. | --- ### 3. Financial Structure – “How do we price, budget, and measure ROI?” | Item | Approach | Example Numbers | |------|----------|-----------------| | **Subscription Fee** | • Per‑seat annual fee (e.g., $1,200/seat).
• Tiered discounts for larger sites. | • 12 hospitals × 50 seats = 600 seats → $720k/year. | | **Implementation Cost** | • One‑time: data integration ($30k), training ($15k), change management ($10k). | • Total ≈ $55k per site; amortized over 3 years. | | **Operating Expense (OPEX)** | • Cloud hosting, vendor support, model updates. | • $5k/month = $60k/year. | | **Capital vs Operating** | • Treat subscription as OPEX to preserve capital for other initiatives. | • Tax‑deferred benefit: 30% tax shield on $720k → $216k savings. | | **Cost‑Savings Model** | • Early sepsis detection reduces ICU LOS by 1 day (average cost $5,000).
• Assume 10% of patients flagged correctly and treated early.
• 12 hospitals × 2000 admissions/year = 24,000; 10% → 2,400 cases. | • Savings: 2,400 × $5k = $12M/yr. | | **Net Present Value (NPV)** | • Discount rate 8%, horizon 3 yrs.
• NPV ≈ $12M – ($720k + $55k) ≈ $11.2M. | • Payback < 1 year. | | **Risk‑Sharing / Performance Contract** | • Offer a “value‑based” clause: if sepsis mortality falls by > 5%, pay an additional bonus to vendor. | • Align incentives, reduce perceived risk. | | **Budgeting & Forecasting** | • Include subscription in the annual IT budget.
• Create a dashboard that tracks actual vs projected savings. | • Monthly KPI report for finance leadership. | --- ### 4. Governance & Oversight – “Who decides what happens?” 1. **Steering Committee (SC)** *Members*: Chief Medical Officer, CIO, CMO, Legal Counsel, Finance VP, Data Science Lead, Clinical Champion from each hospital. *Meetings*: Monthly for the first 6 months, then quarterly. 2. **Model Review Board (MRB)** *Role*: Approve any model retraining or threshold change. *Process*: Submit a “Change Request” with performance data; SC votes 2/3 approval. 3. **Incident Response Team** *Composition*: Clinical Lead, Risk Manager, IT Security, Legal. *Trigger*: Any adverse event linked to the tool. 4. **Audit & Compliance** *External audit* (e.g., SOC 2) annually. *Internal audit* of data lineage and model logs quarterly. --- ### 5. Implementation Roadmap (12‑Month Timeline) | Month | Milestone | |-------|-----------| | 1–2 | Data extraction, retrospective validation, vendor contract finalization. | | 3 | FDA clearance submission (or confirmation of existing clearance). | | 4 | Pilot deployment in 2 hospitals; training rollout. | | 5 | Collect pilot data; adjust thresholds; finalize UI. | | 6 | Full‑scale deployment to all 12 sites; go‑live. | | 7–9 | Continuous monitoring, first quarterly performance review. | | 10 | First model update (if needed) approved by MRB. | | 11 | Financial KPI report; ROI calculation. | | 12 | Annual audit; plan for next version (v2). | --- ## Bottom Line A defensible v1 is **not just a “plug‑and‑play” subscription**; it is an integrated system that: * **Demonstrates clinical efficacy** through rigorous validation and real‑time monitoring. * **Mitigates legal risk** by aligning with FDA SaMD pathways, HIPAA safeguards, and robust vendor indemnification. * **Delivers clear financial value** via a subscription model that is offset by measurable savings in sepsis outcomes. By following the above framework, the health system can launch confidently, scale responsibly, and position itself for future upgrades (e.g., incorporating explainability dashboards or expanding to other predictive domains).
